title.zh: 永磁环表面电流丝离散

summary: Represent a rectangular permanent-ring cross-section by two ordered sets of eight cylindrical surface filaments with opposite dimensionless weights.

identity.relation: rectangular permanent-ring section to weighted surface-filament geometry
identity.direction: section center, width, height and angle -> ordered R-Z points and relative weights
identity.definition: Place eight evenly spaced Z coordinates on each of the two R faces at r0-width/2 and r0+width/2. The first face receives weight -1 per filament and the second +1. Optionally rotate all points about (r0,z0) using the maintained row-vector R-Z convention; weights and order do not change. The function delegates geometry to the maintained MagnetRing with its default sixteen signed weights and returns copied arrays. Every nonzero finite angle is rotated; no small-angle snap is used.
identity.model: fixed 16-filament geometric approximation to opposing permanent-ring surface currents
identity.geometry: rectangular ring cross-section represented by circular filaments in an axisymmetric R-Z drawing
identity.coordinates: cylindrical radius R and axial coordinate Z; positive angle uses the source row-vector convention, clockwise in the standard R-Z drawing
identity.boundary: All generated coordinates must remain finite and radii nonnegative. Any nonzero finite angle uses clockwise degree rotation, including tiny angles; zero alone takes the unrotated path.
assumptions: The returned weights are relative and dimensionless, not current amplitudes in amperes.
The caller supplies SI metre dimensions and applies any physical magnetization/current scaling separately.

inputs.name: r0
inputs.description: Radial coordinate of the section centroid.
inputs.constraints: Finite and nonnegative; resulting filament radii must remain nonnegative.

inputs.name: z0
inputs.description: Axial coordinate of the section centroid.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Separation of the two radial surface-filament groups.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Axial extent spanned by eight points on each group before rotation.

inputs.name: mu_hat_deg
inputs.description: Cross-section rotation about its centroid using the maintained row-vector sign convention.
inputs.constraints: Finite scalar degrees; every nonzero angle is rotated. Large-angle trigonometric argument reduction inherits float64 accuracy.

outputs.name: rz_pts
outputs.constraints: Finite, nonnegative-radius points; first eight negative-weight face, last eight positive-weight face, with unchanged ordering through rotation.

outputs.name: default_weights
outputs.description: Dimensionless relative source weights in point order.
outputs.constraints: Eight -1 entries followed by eight +1 entries; sum is zero.

preconditions: The fixed two-face, eight-points-per-face representation is suitable for the caller's model.
Section dimensions use metres and the generated geometry does not cross R=0.
supported: Ordered surface-filament geometry and relative weights for the maintained axisymmetric permanent-ring approximation.
excluded: Physical magnetization strength, material response or a resolved surface-current density.
Variable filament counts or nonrectangular ring sections.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: ValueError for nonfinite scalar inputs, nonpositive dimensions, negative center radius, or any generated nonfinite/negative-radius coordinate.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: No silent geometry fallback. Generation overflow is rejected through coordinate validation; NumPy/conversion errors propagate. Large finite angles avoid unnecessary pi-times-angle overflow but retain float64 argument-reduction limits.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; no iteration is performed.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No result dictionary is returned when validation raises.

example.description: Check unrotated face ordering, axial span and opposite relative weights.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.field import discretize_permanent_ring
result = discretize_permanent_ring(2.0, 3.0, 4.0, 2.0)
assert result['rz_pts'].shape == (16, 2)
np.testing.assert_allclose(result['rz_pts'][:8, 0], 0.0)
np.testing.assert_allclose(result['rz_pts'][8:, 0], 4.0)
np.testing.assert_allclose(result['rz_pts'][:8, 1], np.linspace(2.0, 4.0, 8))
np.testing.assert_allclose(result['default_weights'], [-1.0]*8 + [1.0]*8)
example.expected: Sixteen [R,Z] points in two ordered groups of eight, with -1 then +1 relative weights.

scope: Unrotated two-face ordering, Z spacing and relative weight signs.
Ninety-degree rotation about the centroid with the maintained sign convention.
Axis-crossing and nonfinite geometry rejection, exact tiny-angle rotation, and finite generation at a very large finite angle.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Targeted source regressions, explicit analytic fixtures and a selected no-source installed-wheel replay cover this finite contract. No arbitrary physical-model suitability, continuum convergence, human scientific endorsement or redistribution permission is inferred.
known_limitations: Exactly sixteen filament points and fixed relative weights are returned.
The result does not encode absolute current or magnetization strength.
Large-angle finiteness is checked, but float64 argument reduction does not certify arbitrary huge-angle phase accuracy.
